newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African ANC maps moderate path for new millennium.
newsitem.headline: S.African ANC maps moderate path for new millennium.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela's ruling African National Congress (ANC) has mapped a moderate course for the new millennium in a draft strategy document prepared for a major congress in December.
The ratification of Deputy President Thabo Mbeki as the new party leader and, by implication, Mandela's heir apparent, will be the major decision of the ANC's 50th national conference.

But the gathering of several hundred former guerrillas and activists will also have to adopt a strategy to consolidate the power it won from the white National Party in the first all-race elections in 1994.
"The foundation has been laid for our society to develop into a truly non-racial, non-sexist and united nation," party leaders said in a document released to the media on Thursday.
"However...the realities of inequality, poverty and underdevelopment have become more obvious."

ANC spokesman Ronnie Mamoepa said the document, entitled "All Power to the People", would be circulated amongst party branches and organisations for refinement and discussion ahead of the conference, which begins on December 21.
The draft maps a moderate path into the future with the role of whites in the party and in South African society reaffirmed.
"The white communities are not an exclusive terrain of parties opposed to change. A new sense of proud belonging constitutes a strong element that should be harnessed.
"The ANC must win over to its side those who previously benefited from the system of apartheid," the document says.
The reaffirmation of the ANC's commitment to non-racialism appears to repudiate the rising Africanist lobby within the 85-year-old organisation.
The document shuns the renewed popularity of the label "African" sometimes used to distinguish black from white, saying:
"The overarching identity of being a South African must be promoted among all those who are indeed South African."

Leading ANC members have confirmed to Reuters that there is a growing resistance to the prominence of white, Asian and mixed-race coloured officials and decision-makers in the party and in the upper ranks of government.
The document also clearly reaffirms the ANC's tolerance of Afrikaner and other minority groups with a renewed commitment to racial, ethnic, language, religious and cultural equality.
ANC leftists accuse white Afrikaners opposed to change of using culture, language and religion as smoke-screens for a campaign to preserve their apartheid privileges.
The document acknowledges that capitalism will dominate global economics, but says African nations could help to ensure that market imperatives take account of the needs of the poor.
